findings.quote:
2.3 Permitted Disclosures. The Receiving Party shall not disclose or make available any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party to any third party, except that the Receiving Party may disclose such Confidential Information to those of its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the Purpose, provided that:
2.3.1 prior to any such disclosure, the Receiving Party informs each such Representative of the confidential nature of the information;
2.3.2 each such Representative is bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality no less protective of the Confidential Information than the terms set forth in this Agreement; and
2.3.3 the Receiving Party shall be wholly responsible and liable to the Disclosing Party for any act or omission of any of its Representatives that would constitute a breach of this Agreement if committed by the Receiving Party directly.

findings.quote: 1.1.2 "Confidential Information" means any and all non-public, proprietary, or confidential information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party or its Affiliates (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party or its Affiliates (the "Receiving Party"), whether orally, visually, electronically, in writing, or in any other tangible or intangible form, that is designated as "Confidential," "Proprietary," or with a similar legend at the time of disclosure, or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances surrounding its disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes software, source code, object code, APIs, system architectures, algorithms, product roadmaps, technical specifications, customer lists, pricing models, financial data, business plans, marketing strategies, and any notes, analyses, compilations, studies, or other documents prepared by the Receiving Party or its Representatives to the extent they contain or reflect such information.
